### 1. Research & Evaluation of 4-Person Formats, Handicap Allowances & Scoring Rules

To design the fairest and most enjoyable setup for your 16-player golf day, we researched and compared seven official rules and editorial golf sources covering 4-person formats, USGA handicap allocation formulas, pace of play, and tie-breaking procedures:

1. **USGA Rules of Handicapping — Appendix C: Handicap Allowances** (`https://www.usga.org/.../Appendix%20C%20Handicap%20Allowances.htm`)
2. **USGA Committee Guide — Scramble Formats & Calculations (Rule 7, LG_R7h5)** (`https://www.usga.org/.../LG_R7h5.htm`)
3. **USGA Committee Guide — Shamble Formats & Allowances (Rule 7, LG_R7h7)** (`https://www.usga.org/.../LG_R7h7.htm`)
4. **USGA Committee Procedures — Deciding Ties & Matching Scorecards (Rule 7, LG_R7l4 / Section 5A(6))** (`https://www.usga.org/.../LG_R7l4.htm`)
5. **USGA Committee Guide — Multi-Ball & Stroke Play Formats (Rule 7, LG_R7g1)** (`https://www.usga.org/.../LG_R7g1.htm`)
6. **Golf Digest Outing Guide — "How to Pick the Right Format for Your Golf Outing"** (`https://www.golfdigest.com/story/how-to-pick-the-right-format-for-your-golf-outing`)
7. **The R&A — Appendix C: Handicap Allowances (WHS Reference)** (`https://www.randa.org/roh/appendices/appendix-c`)

#### Comparison of 4-Person Formats for Exactly 4 Teams of 4

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **4-Person Scramble** *(Selected Format)* | All 4 tee off, pick the best shot; all 4 play from that spot until holed. | **25% low / 20% / 15% / 10% high** of Course Handicap (deducted from team gross). | **No (with guardrails):** In raw gross play low handicaps dominate, but the USGA weighted allowance plus a **mandatory 3-drive minimum per player** prevents single-player dominance and gives higher handicaps critical moments to shine. | **Easiest & Fastest:** 1 gross score per hole. Errant balls are abandoned immediately; round takes **4:00–4:15**. Zero pressure on beginners. |
| **4-Person Shamble (Bramble)** *(Alternative 1)* | All 4 tee off, select the best drive; each golfer plays their own ball into the hole from there. | **65% of Course Handicap** for 4-person teams (USGA LG_R7h7). Best 1 or 2 net balls count. | **Moderate:** Low handicappers gain birdie chances from ideal fairway drives, while high handicappers get 65% strokes on approach/putt. | **Moderate:** 4 individual scorecards kept from the 2nd shot inward. Slower than a scramble; 16+ handicaps can still struggle around greens. |
| **2 Best Balls of 4 (Four-Ball Alliance)** *(Alternative 2)* | Everyone plays their own ball from tee to green on every hole. Sum the 2 best net scores. | **85% of Course Handicap** (USGA Appendix C). | **Can favor high handicappers:** High handicaps who make sporadic net birdies/eagles often overpower steady pars from scratch golfers. | **Complex & Slow:** 4 balls in play constantly; requires looking for lost balls in woods. Can easily exceed **5+ hours** with 16–18 handicappers. |
| **ChaChaCha / 1-2-3 Best Ball** | Rotation: 1 best net on Hole 1, 2 best net on Hole 2, 3 best net on Hole 3; repeat cycle. | **80%–85% of Course Handicap**. | **Moderate:** Demands that high handicaps produce scores on the "3-ball" holes. | **Confusing:** Players constantly lose track of which hole requires how many counting balls; risks scorecard errors. |

### 2. Single Best Format Recommendation & Why It Fits

**Selected Format: 4-Person Team Scramble with a Mandatory 3-Drive Minimum**

**Why it fits this specific 16-player field better than the alternatives:**
1. **Extreme Skill Disparity:** Your roster ranges from scratch/near-scratch golfers (**Cody: 1, C: 3, Greg: 4, Dave: 4, Johnny: 4, Sal: 4**) to high-recreational players (**Eric: 16, Doric: 17, Marcus: 18**). In individual or Best Ball stroke play, high handicappers feel intimidated, lose balls, and spend the round grinding through double bogeys. A scramble allows high handicappers to roll in clutch putts or hit key fairways without ever feeling like they are holding up the group.
2. **Pace of Play for 4 Foursomes:** With 16 players in 4 consecutive tee times, maintaining momentum is paramount. A scramble eliminates ball-hunting in hazards and out-of-bounds, ensuring all four groups finish within **4 hours to 4 hours and 15 minutes**.
3. **The Essential Drive Rule Guardrail:** By enforcing that **each team must use at least 3 tee shots from each of its 4 players**, you neutralize the risk of a low handicapper like Cody (1) hitting 14 drives. Teams must strategically use their higher handicappers' straight drives early on par 4s or par 3s, making every player feel valued.

### 3. Official Tournament Rules & Procedures

* **Scoring Method:** **18-Hole Team Net Stroke Play Scramble**.
  * Each foursome records one gross team score per hole. At the end of the round, the team's official USGA Playing Handicap is subtracted from the total gross score to determine the Final Net Score.
  * *Lie Rule:* The team may place their ball within **one club-length** of the selected ball, no closer to the hole, maintaining the same condition (rough remains in rough, fairway in fairway, sand in bunker). On the putting green, balls are placed within **6 inches** of the ball-marker.
  * *Drive Rule:* Minimum of **3 tee shots per golfer** must be recorded on the official scorecard.
* **Handicap Allowance Rule:** **Official USGA Rules of Handicapping (Appendix C)**
  $$\text{Team Playing Handicap} = (25\% \times \text{Lowest Hcp}) + (20\% \times \text{2nd Lowest}) + (15\% \times \text{3rd Lowest}) + (10\% \times \text{Highest Hcp})$$
* **Tie-Break Procedure:** **USGA Committee Procedures Section 5A(6) (Scorecard Matching)**
  * If two or more teams tie for 1st place on net score:
    1. **Best Net Score on the Back 9 (Holes 10–18)**, deducting $\frac{1}{2}$ of the team's playing handicap.
    2. If still tied: **Best Net Score on the Last 6 Holes (Holes 13–18)**, deducting $\frac{1}{3}$ of the handicap.
    3. If still tied: **Best Net Score on the Last 3 Holes (Holes 16–18)**, deducting $\frac{1}{6}$ of the handicap.
    4. If still tied: **Best Net Score on Hole 18**, deducting $\frac{1}{18}$ of the handicap.
    5. If still tied: Sudden-death 1-putt or chip-off at the practice green.
